title: Which shops lie below the ground?
description: A picture of the tall block shows a ground line with teal floors above it and amber floors under it. The shops on the amber floors are read one by one from the line downwards, then the floor on the line is read. Keeko thinks all the shops are above the ground, and the count of amber floors breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: a ground line splits the floors into those above it, the one on it, and those below it. Watch for students who think a floor can only go up.

source: Observe that some of the floors in the 'Building of Fun' are
video_script.why: A child learns that floors can lie below the ground and reads the shops on them from the picture.
video_script.substitution: the floors of the book's own tall block of shops, read from the picture
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_10}}: the tall block of shops with a ground line, teal floors above and amber floors below
video_script.wrong_answer: all the shops are above the ground
video_script.wrong_move: counts only the floors above the ground line and forgets the floors under it
video_script.payoff_line: The ground floor holds the Welcome Hall.

final_answer.value: Below the ground: Toy Store, Video Games, Cinema, Ghost House, Dinosaur. Ground floor: Welcome Hall.
final_answer.spoken: the Toy Store, the Video Games shop, the Cinema Centre, the Ghost House and the Dinosaur floor, and the Welcome Hall on the ground floor

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: below the ground, Toy Store, Video Games, Cinema, Ghost House, Dinosaur; ground floor, Welcome Hall
maths_rules: Floors below the ground, from the line downwards: Toy Store, Video Games shop, Cinema Centre, Ghost House, Dinosaur floor.
That is five floors under the ground line (the book: six floors above and five below).
The floor on the ground line is the Welcome Hall.
video_script.design: One idea: the ground line splits the floors. One picture throughout; teal above the line, amber below it. Keeko's doubt is broken by counting the amber floors.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks all the shops are above the ground, because a tall block only goes up.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But count the amber floors one by one, and five of them lie under the line.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A floor can lie below the ground, and each of those floors holds a shop.
